nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - red-test-quality-audit [ses_f24da1859ffekbCFrUqlOXa11m].md:L1425] The test never touches production code. It calls `captureYtEventsMulti()` (443–454) and then hand-constructs two players itself (1177–1188) with its **own** fresh `events: { onReady: () => {}, onStateChange: () => {}, onError: () => {} }` literals. Line 1190 (`toHaveLength(2)`) only proves `all.push` ran twice, which the two explicit `make()` calls guarantee. Lines 1192–1193 (`all[0].onError !== all[1].onError`) compare two distinct arrow-function literals the test itself authored at 1181–1183; JS guarantees they differ, so the assertion is unfalsifiable by anything in the production file.

nodes.label: A toContain substring match does not prove the message belongs to that specific error code
nodes.norm_label: a tocontain substring match does not prove the message belongs to that specific error code
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - red-test-quality-audit [ses_f24da1859ffekbCFrUqlOXa11m].md:L1436] - **Line 1208 substring-matches, it does not identify the code.** `toContain("2")` is satisfied by `"YouTube error 2"`, by an implementation that returns the same message for every code, or by one that returns the whole code list. Nothing proves the message belongs to *that* code. Fix: assert the per-code message differs across iterations (e.g. collect into a `Set` and assert `size === YT_ERROR_CODES.length`), and drop the vacuous `not.toBe`.

nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - r6-t2-red-validity-review [ses_f1cff10ceffeUXB4uK4ZHe4gtZ].md:L1576] - **C `selection_contract_capture_predicate` — cannot be RED; spec-lock at best.** No such function exists, so the file does not compile, which kills the whole target: **A never executes and the recorded RED can never be exit 100.** Worse, A/B/C/D written together mean the single Step 1 command can only ever produce 101 with 0 tests run, contradicting §6 line 492 ("100 or 101") and the plan's claim that A then fails with left `"clip"`. A truth table over a function the same commit invents is green by construction unless a row is derived from a documented existing violation — the only such row is `(false, true, false) → false` (today that path still backs up, sleeps, and snapshots the clipboard, producing the corruption), and the plan never states that row.
